allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Daigo, a cellist, is laid off from his orchestra and moves with his wife back to his small hometown where the living is cheaper. Thinking he’s applying for a job at a travel agency he finds he’s being interviewed for work with departures of a more permanent nature – as an undertaker’s assistant.

facts.title: Departures

semanticBoundaryFlags.message: Deliberate 130-minute drama could be argued as slow or medium; slow chosen given the grief-ritual premise, but human review is advised.
Alone and family both grounded; whether family viewing suits death-centered content warrants review.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Expecting a routine desk job, an unemployed musician inadvertently steps into the solemn, intimate world of preparing the deceased for their final journey.
visibleEditorialCopy.description: After his orchestra disbands, cellist Daigo returns with his wife to his small hometown. Looking for steady work, an interview for what seems like a travel agency instead places him as an assistant to an undertaker.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: A slow, thoughtful Japanese drama with heavy emotional weight, rewarding patient and engaged viewing.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by Yojiro Takita, this reflective drama handles grief and vocation with quiet tenderness, finding unexpected dignity in the delicate rituals of saying goodbye.
